subject.title: Standardize async resource lifecycle management across retry/cleanup paths

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared lifecycle primitive for async drain/cancel semantics, and should that contract live in core gateway/session runtime, embedded agent runtime, or the plugin SDK?
rationale: Current main already has targeted lifecycle helpers, so the remaining change is an ownership and public-contract decision rather than a narrow source repair.

options.title: Design a narrow shared lifecycle contract
options.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner-approved design that names the API boundary, shutdown ordering, timeout behavior, and representative migrations before implementation.

options.title: Continue localized lifecycle helpers
options.body: Treat the existing session admission, embedded cleanup, channel helper, and plugin cleanup mechanisms as the preferred pattern and close only after maintainers reject a shared primitive.

options.title: Defer until a new concrete failure
options.body: Leave broad consolidation unscheduled and require a fresh reproducible lifecycle bug before expanding core or SDK API surface.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow shared lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner-approved design that names the API boundary, shutdown ordering, timeout behavior, and representative migrations before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current-main routing candidate across the embedded cleanup, gateway/channel, and session lifecycle surfaces involved in a shared contract decision.
